title: Regional Finance Controller - Kenya
description:
Location: Nairobi, Kenya (for exceptional candidates, we are open to other countries where IRW has a country office in the African region) Contract: Permanent Salary: £38,322 Closing Date: 11th October 2026 Islamic Relief Worldwide (IRW) is a faith-based humanitarian and development organisation working to save and transform the lives of some of the world's most vulnerable people. Established in 1984 and operating in over 45 countries, we respond to emergencies, tackle poverty, empower communities, and advocate for lasting change. We are seeking an experienced and strategic Regional Finance Controller - Africa (West and East) to join our Finance & Corporate Services Division. This is a unique opportunity for a senior finance leader who is passionate about financial governance, capacity building, compliance, and driving sustainable improvement across complex international operations. The preferred location for this role is Nairobi, Kenya. However, we recognise that exceptional talent exists across the continent and will consider applications from suitably qualified candidates located within Africa who can support the regional travel requirements and responsibilities of the position. The Finance & Corporate Services Division is a strategic enabler of organisational performance, accountability and sustainability, delivering integrated services across Finance, Treasury, ERP & Digital Transformation, ICT, Supply Chain and Facilities. As part of an ambitious finance transformation programme, the division is strengthening financial governance, independent oversight, service excellence, and data-driven decision making across the organisation's global footprint. About the Role The Regional Finance Controller (RFC) is responsible for providing financial oversight, governance, assurance, compliance, and capacity building across Islamic Relief's country offices and implementing partners throughout West and East Africa. This is far more than a traditional financial control role. You will work closely with Country Directors, Finance Managers, operational teams, and local partners to strengthen financial management practices, build organisational capability, and ensure the highest standards of financial stewardship are embedded across the region. You will play a critical leadership role in improving financial performance, enhancing internal control frameworks, strengthening donor and statutory compliance, and supporting long-term financial sustainability. Through visible, hands-on engagement with country offices and partners, you will help drive a step-change in financial discipline, transparency, accountability, and decision-making. The role combines strategic oversight with practical delivery. You will be responsible for assessing financial performance, mentoring regional finance teams, identifying and mitigating risk, supporting fraud prevention initiatives, and ensuring finance effectively supports programme delivery and donor confidence. Reporting to the Global Finance Operations Lead, you will provide expert technical guidance and leadership across a diverse and complex regional portfolio, supporting the ongoing evolution of Islamic Relief's global finance operating model. The successful candidate will spend approximately 50% of their time travelling across the region, providing direct support to country offices, finance teams, and implementing partners. The Successful Candidate Will Have: A professionally recognised accounting qualification (ACCA, CIMA, ICAEW, ICMA or equivalent). Significant senior-level financial management experience, ideally within the humanitarian, NGO, development, or international non-profit sector. Demonstrable experience leading financial governance, compliance, assurance, and internal control activities across multiple entities or geographical locations. Strong expertise in budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling, financial planning, and scenario analysis. Experience producing consolidated management accounts, variance analysis, financial performance reporting, and strategic financial insight. Proven experience managing donor compliance requirements and statutory obligations. A strong understanding of financial risk management, fraud prevention, and control frameworks. Experience leading, developing, mentoring, and coaching finance teams. Excellent stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence and support both finance and non-finance leaders. Strong communication skills and the ability to present complex financial information clearly and effectively. Experience designing and delivering finance training, capability building, and development programmes. High levels of integrity, accountability, professionalism, and cultural sensitivity. Commitment to the mission, vision, and values of Islamic Relief Worldwide. Fluency in both English and French. Desirable Experience managing donor-funded programmes and institutional grant reporting within international NGOs. Experience working in fragile, conflict-affected, or complex operating environments. Strong understanding of the geopolitical, regulatory, and socio-economic contexts across Africa. Experience supporting finance transformation, organisational change, or continuous improvement initiatives. Experience working with local implementing partners and sub-grantees. Why Join Islamic Relief? This role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact across multiple countries by strengthening financial performance, governance, accountability, and sustainability throughout one of the world's leading humanitarian organisations. If you are a strategic finance leader who enjoys developing people, improving systems, driving compliance, and enabling operational excellence across international programmes, we would love to hear from you. For more information, please refer to the full Job Description and Person Specification. If you are talented, reliable, service-minded, resilient, and highly motivated, with a strong commitment to Islamic Relief's mission and values of Sincerity, Excellence, Compassion, Social Justice, and Custodianship, please submit your application via our online recruitment portal. PLEASE NOTE: Interviews may be held on an ongoing basis, and we reserve the right to close this vacancy prior to the advertised closing date should a suitable candidate be identified. Pre-Employment Checks Any employment with Islamic Relief will be subject to: Proof of eligibility to live and work within the UK. Satisfactory references. Appropriate screening and safeguarding checks. Please note that we are only able to consider applications from candidates who already have the right to work in the UK. Sponsorship is not available for this position. Our Values and Commitment to Safeguarding Islamic Relief is committed to preventing all forms of abuse, exploitation, harassment, discrimination, and financial misconduct. We expect all employees and volunteers to share this commitment and uphold the highest standards of conduct. All appointments are subject to satisfactory references and safeguarding checks, including participation in the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme where applicable. Islamic Relief is an equal opportunities employer.

How to Apply: **For further details about the role and application requirements, please refer to the full Job Description and Person Specification and apply via our online recruitment portal using the link below.** [**Regional Finance Controller**](https://islamic-relief.current-vacancies.com/Jobs/Advert/4327242?cid=1858&t=Regional-Finance-Controller)

title: RESPONSABLE DU BUREAU DE PLAIDOYER ET DE LIAISON AUPRÈS DE L’UNION AFRICAINE, Oxfam en Afrique
description:
Type de contrat : Contrat à durée déterminée de 2 ans Grade interne : B1, International Rémunération : conforme à la grille salariale d’Oxfam International. Cette offre comprend les avantages sociaux de base ainsi que les prestations globales applicables au personnel recruté à l’international et relocalisé.Nous considérons que les modalités de travail flexibles sont essentielles pour bâtir le Secrétariat de demain. Nous sommes donc disposés à échanger avec vous sur les modalités susceptibles de vous convenir. Le poste Oxfam en Afrique recherche une personne expérimentée, dotée d’un leadership reconnu et d’un forte capacité d’influence, pour diriger son Bureau de plaidoyer et de liaison auprès de l’Union africaine (UA), basé à Addis-Abeba. En tant que membre de l’Équipe de direction de la Plateforme Afrique, vous piloterez l’engagement d’Oxfam auprès de l’Union africaine et de ses institutions. Vous élaborerez et mettrez en œuvre des stratégies de plaidoyer à fort impact afin d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques à l’échelle continentale. Vous représenterez Oxfam au plus haut niveau auprès de l’UA, nouerez des relations stratégiques et contribuerez à positionner Oxfam comme un partenaire crédible et de confiance. Ce poste joue un rôle central dans la réalisation de la mission d’Oxfam en Afrique : il établit un lien entre les espaces d’élaboration des politiques continentales et les réalités nationales, tout en veillant à ce que les actions de plaidoyer soient cohérentes, porteuses d’impact et ancrées dans les réalités vécues par les communautés. Ce poste relève de la Direction Afrique, avec un rattachement matriciel à la Direction Plaidoyer, Campagnes et Engagement (ACE). Profil recherché Nous recherchons une personne reconnue pour son leadership en matière de plaidoyer et d’influence, disposant d’une solide expérience de collaboration avec l’Union africaine ou des institutions multilatérales comparables. Vous avez démontré votre capacité à concevoir et à mettre en œuvre des stratégies d’influence porteuses d’impact, combinant analyse des politiques, plaidoyer, communication médiatique et partenariats afin de favoriser des changements significatifs. Vous excellez dans l’établissement de relations et la négociation, savez évoluer efficacement dans des environnements complexes associant de multiples parties prenantes et êtes en mesure d’exercer une influence au plus haut niveau. Grâce à votre capacité de réflexion stratégique et d’analyse politique, vous savez traduire les processus de l’UA en possibilités concrètes d’influence et d’impact pour les pays et les partenaires. Votre expérience du leadership vous permet de diriger des équipes diversifiées et de travailler au sein d’un réseau mondial, tout en favorisant la collaboration et la redevabilité. Vous avez une connaissance approfondie du contexte sociopolitique africain et adhérez aux approches féministes, décoloniales et portées par les partenaires. La maîtrise professionnelle de l’anglais et du français est indispensable. Pourquoi nous rejoindre Ce poste offre une occasion rare d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques au plus haut niveau continental. À Oxfam, vous façonnerez notre engagement auprès de l’Union africaine, piloterez le plaidoyer sur des enjeux majeurs tels que les inégalités, la pauvreté et la justice, et collaborerez avec des gouvernements, des diplomates et des institutions internationales pour réaliser des changements concrets. Au sein d’une équipe de direction diversifiée et collaborative, vous contribuerez à rapprocher les politiques continentales des réalités des communautés, afin que les décisions prises au plus haut niveau se traduisent par des résultats tangibles pour les populations partout en Afrique. Ce que nous offrons À Oxfam, nous sommes convaincus que chaque aspect de notre travail peut contribuer à un changement positif. Si vous partagez cette conviction et possédez les compétences nécessaires pour relever les défis liés à ce poste, cette fonction vous offrira de grandes possibilités d’épanouissement personnel ainsi que d’excellentes perspectives d’évolution professionnelle. Oxfam s’engage à proposer une rémunération équitable, sur la base d’une semaine de travail de 36 heures À propos de nous Oxfam est un mouvement mondial de personnes qui agissent ensemble pour mettre fin à l’injustice qu’est la pauvreté. Cela signifie que nous nous attaquons aux inégalités qui maintiennent les populations dans la pauvreté. Ensemble, nous sauvons des vies, protégeons les populations et les aidons à reconstruire leur existence. Lorsqu’une catastrophe survient, nous aidons les personnes à bâtir un avenir meilleur, pour elles-mêmes et pour les autres. Nous agissons sur des enjeux tels que les droits fonciers, le changement climatique et les discriminations à l’égard des femmes. Et nous ne nous arrêterons pas tant que chaque personne sur la planète ne pourra pas vivre à l’abri de la pauvreté. Nous sommes une confédération internationale composée de 22 organisations affiliées et du Secrétariat d’Oxfam International. Avec nos partenaires et les communautés locales, nous menons des actions humanitaires, des programmes de développement et des campagnes dans plus de 76 pays. Oxfam en Afrique (OiA) est une plateforme continentale qui assure la coordination des bureaux pays d’Oxfam en Afrique et collabore avec des organisations de la société civile, des universitaires, des gouvernements et le secteur privé afin de contribuer à une Afrique plus égalitaire, en remettant en cause les structures de pouvoir qui perpétuent les inégalités et les injustices. À cette fin, Oxfam en Afrique apporte un leadership intellectuel dynamique et offre un espace de collaboration à ses partenaires. Oxfam en Afrique joue un rôle moteur dans l’appui aux communautés locales et le renforcement de leur pouvoir d’agir, la promotion de l’égalité de genre, le plaidoyer en faveur de changements de politiques publiques et le renforcement des capacités des organisations locales de la société civile. L’ensemble de notre travail est guidé par nos valeurs fondamentales : Autonomisation, Redevabilité, Inclusion, Courage, Solidarité et Égalité. Notre engagement en matière de safeguarding (Protection contre le harcèlement, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels) Oxfam s’engage à prévenir toute forme de comportement inapproprié au travail, notamment le harcèlement sexuel, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels, les manquements à l’intégrité et les irrégularités financières, ainsi qu’à promouvoir le bien-être des enfants, des jeunes et des adultes. Oxfam attend de l’ensemble de son personnel et de ses volontaires qu’ils partagent cet engagement et respectent notre Code de conduite. Nous accordons une importance primordiale au recrutement de personnes qui partagent nos valeurs et les mettent en pratique. Remarque : Toute offre d’emploi sera subordonnée à la réception de références satisfaisantes et pourra faire l’objet de contrôles appropriés, notamment une vérification du casier judiciaire et des contrôles relatifs au financement du terrorisme. description:
WHAT IS IMPACT INITIATIVES ? OUR AIM: IMPACT aims to shape practices and influence policies in humanitarian and development settings, in order to positively impact the lives of people and their communities. Created in 2010, IMPACT is a Geneva-based NGO and the largest independent data provider in contexts of crisis. We aim to support a range of stakeholders in making better, more informed decisions in humanitarian, stabilisation, and development settings. We believe that a key pathway to better planning and decision-making is direct engagement with local communities. HOW DO WE WORK ? IMPACT takes an initiative-based approach to structuring our programming. Each initiative has a specific aim, operational model, and portfolio of solutions. REACH strengthens evidence-based humanitarian decision-making through efficient data collection, management, and analysis - before, during, and after an emergency. PANDA improves the impact of humanitarian and development interventions through programme design, assessments, and monitoring & evaluation. AGORA promotes localised and multi-sectoral aid action in support of the recovery and stabilisation of crisis-affected communities, in partnership with local stakeholders Through our global team of research specialists, on average IMPACT publishes more than 1,700 information products on a yearly basis. In 2010, IMPACT was launched at the initiative of ACTED, an international NGO whose headquarters are based in Paris and is present in thirty countries. The two organizations have a strong complementarity formalized in a global partnership, which particularly allows IMPACT to benefit from ACTED’s operational support in its fields of intervention. We are currently looking for a Country Representative to lead our Ethiopia mission, based in Addis Abeba Position: Country Representative Contract duration: 12 months Location: Addis Abeba, Ethiopia, with potential travel to Kampala, Uganda Starting Date: October / November 2026 Application Deadline: 09 October 2026. COUNTRY PROFILE Since 2018, Ethiopia has experienced escalating insecurity and unrest, including large-scale displacement, loss of life, and widespread destruction of property, following significant domestic political changes. These crises have compounded the effects of recurring climate-related shocks affecting large parts of the country. In November 2020, conflict erupted in the northern Tigray region, triggering significant displacement across Tigray, Amhara, and Afar regions. Since August 2023, renewed conflict in Amhara has further intensified humanitarian needs, leading to the declaration of a state of emergency and restrictions on movement across the region. Together, these crises have severely disrupted livelihoods, constrained access to essential goods and staple commodities, and increased the vulnerability of affected populations, placing additional pressure on humanitarian response capacities across the country. FUNCTIONS Under the management of IMPACT’s Regional Coordinator (RC) for Africa in Geneva, the Country Representative (CR) is responsible for representing IMPACT and managing and developing IMPACT’s programmes in Ethiopia. S/he leads the IMPACT team to achieve program excellence and ensure the highest level of impact and accountability, while ensuring compliance to IMPACT guidelines, policies and standards across the mission. The CR is in regular contact with HQ, ensuring that organizational risks are promptly and clearly communicated to the Regional Coordinator and other relevant HQ Senior Management. S/he will promote organizational vision and core values across the mission and will actively link with HQ to contribute to the implementation of IMPACT’s global strategy. In his/her mission, the Country Representative will be hosted by Acted and will fall under the direct responsibility and management of Acted’s Country Director for all Administrative, Security, Logistics and Finance issues. S/he will therefore fully abide by Acted’s Security, HR, Administration and Logistics rules and regulations, and, in coordination with Acted, will ensure that all IMPACT staff abide by them. title: Ethiopia Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer (Fixed-Term)
description:
About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. In Ethiopia, we engage farmers in agroforestry and community-based seed multiplication to increase farmers’ incomes and make farming systems more resilient. Engaging with local actors at every step but bringing innovative ideas from outside, we are making rural farming more market-friendly and environmentally sustainable. The farmers we work with in Ethiopia have planted more than 30 million trees, produced over 1500 metric tonnes of improved teff seed, and improved the futures of nearly 200,000 community members. Our permanent team numbers over 180 with nearly 1,000 rural seasonal staff supporting them. Our country headquarters are in Addis Ababa and we have a large program office in Bahir Dar, plus several smaller field offices. About the Role The Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer supports the Ethiopia Trees Program's expansion through desk research, primary data gathering, field verification scoutings, and evidence generation to identify and assess potential expansion opportunities across Ethiopia. The role synthesizes geographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and stakeholder information to support strategic expansion decisions and operational readiness. The officer will participate in field scouting visits with the expansion team to validate desk research findings and gather additional insights. Responsibilities Data Collection & Research Conduct desk research to identify and assess potential program expansion areas across regions, zones, and woredas. Collect, analyze, and synthesize agricultural, environmental, demographic, socioeconomic, market, and government data to support expansion planning. Review secondary data from government institutions, research organizations, development partners, and other credible sources to generate evidence-based insights. Monitor demographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and policy trends to identify opportunities and potential risks for program expansion. Develop and maintain databases, trackers, and research documentation to support expansion planning and operational readiness. Verify, clean, and analyze research and field data to ensure quality, accuracy, consistency, and usability. Support the development and continuous improvement of expansion assessment tools, scoring frameworks, research methodologies, and analytical processes. Field & Stakeholder Verification of Data Participate in field scouting and assessment visits to validate desk research findings and collect additional information. Engage with government offices, development partners, local stakeholders, and other relevant actors to verify data, assumptions, and findings. Assess key expansion criteria, including agroforestry suitability, water availability, land suitability, market potential, operational feasibility, scalability, accessibility, and implementation risks. Identify data gaps and discrepancies and coordinate with relevant stakeholders to obtain and validate additional information. Integrate field observations and stakeholder feedback with secondary data to strengthen expansion assessments and recommendations. Reporting & Collaboration Prepare clear and evidence-based assessment reports, analytical summaries, and recommendations to support expansion decisions. Present research findings and recommendations to relevant teams and stakeholders and contribute to expansion planning discussions. Collaborate with the expansion team and relevant technical and operational teams to translate research findings into actionable expansion plans. Maintain clear documentation of research findings, field validation results, assumptions, and recommendations to support decision-making and future reference Reporting, Stakeholder Engagement & Collaboration Support engagement with government institutions, community representatives, development partners, and other relevant stakeholders during expansion assessments and field scouting activities. Coordinate information gathering, stakeholder consultations, and validation activities to support expansion planning and decision-making. Identify collaboration opportunities that strengthen expansion planning, field implementation, and operational readiness. Prepare high-quality assessment reports, presentations, briefing materials, and regular progress updates for internal and external stakeholders. Document research findings, field observations, lessons learned, stakeholder feedback, and key decisions to support knowledge sharing and continuous improvement. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to translate research findings and stakeholder insights into actionable recommendations and expansion plans. Track assigned activities and maintain accurate and up-to-date documentation related to expansion research, assessments, and planning. Perform other research and operational support tasks as assigned to advance the Tree Program’s expansion objectives. Support the recruitment of field staff Career Growth and Development We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career. Qualifications Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for . For this role specifically, you will have: Education Bachelor's degree required. Candidates with academic backgrounds in Forestry, Agroforestry, Agriculture, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Science, Geography, Rural Development, Watershed Management, or related fields are preferred. Experience 2 years or more of relevant professional experience in forestry, agroforestry, agriculture, natural resource management, landscape restoration, rural development, field innovation, government relations, or related fields. Experience conducting research, data collection, expansion assessments, market assessments, or strategic planning. Experience working with government institutions, development partners, or community stakeholders. Experience supporting field assessments or validation exercises is an advantage. Willingness to travel to rural and remote locations for field scouting and stakeholder engagement. Skills Strong analytical, research, and problem-solving skills. Excellent data gathering, analysis, and report writing skills. Ability to synthesize complex information into practical recommendations for decision-making. Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills. Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Ability to useMicrosoft Office, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. Experience using digital data collection tools is an advantage. Languages Can communicate in English. Fluency in Amharic. Proficiency in Afaan Oromo is preferred Preferred Start Date As soon as possible Job Location Addis Ababa, Ethiopia Benefits Health insurance, paid time off Contract Duration 1 year Eligibility This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Ethiopia. Please report any suspicious communication here ( globalhotline@oneacrefund.org ), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve. title: Consultant - Final Evaluation Coherence programme Ethiopia
description:
1. Introduction The COHERENCE programme Ethiopia 2022-2026 is implemented by Ethiopian Catholic Church – Social and Development Commission Soddo branch (ECC-SDCO/S) and Adigrat branch (ECC-SDCO/Ad) , with coordination support by the East Africa regional programme Manager CI.be. The programme is implemented in 7 countries and is co-funded by the Belgian Government. The program’s aim is to equip rural communities so that they become more resilient and can better cope with crisis situations. Above all, the program wants the most vulnerable people, particularly women, young people and people with disabilities, to have expanded opportunities to improve their living conditions. Through a ‘triple nexus ’ approach, focus is on (1) social cohesion, peace-building and rights protection within communities; (2) rural economic development; and (3) disaster preparedness The present terms of reference relate exclusively to the final evaluation of COHERENCE Ethiopia. The final evaluations of the three other country programs are the subject of separate tenders and fall outside the scope of this assignment. 2. Object of the evaluation: COHERENCE Ethiopia 2.1 Program objective, results and activities To address food insecurity of poor and vulnerable households – with a focus on female-headed and landless households – of 2 kebeles in Damot Woyde district (Wolaita) and 2 kebeles in Irob district (Eastern Tigray) , COHERENCE Ethiopia aimed to improve their livelihood base in a sustainable way, by means of a triple nexus approach, linking three complementary areas: social cohesion, rural economic development and disaster risk reduction (DRR). The action’s specific objective was formulated as follows: “By the end of 2026, poor and vulnerable households, especially resource poor female-headed and landless households, in two kebeles (Endamosa and Hareze Sabata) of Irob district and two kebeles (Kindo Koyo and Mayo Kote) of Damot Woyde district have strengthened their livelihood basis, better enabling them to seize opportunities and realize their aspirations”. The objective was to be achieved through three results. A first result concerned social cohesion that was to be improved by building household and community capacity to manage resource-induced conflicts and to ensure equitable and fair access or entitlement to natural resources, through, among others: Conducting a rapid gender context analysis at community level (1 in each intervention area); Organizing in groups and training of 180 community cohesion and gender empowerment agents on peace building, conflict management and facilitation skills; Organizing community dialogue sessions on peace and conflict management and gender equity (while applying the household transformation method); Rehabilitating and expanding water piping to address existing water access conflict (Wolaita); Planting tree seedlings on communal land between communities as a joint, social cohesion enhancing activity (Tigray); Providing energy-saving stoves for 300 households (Wolaita). The direct causes of food insecurity in the intervention zones are – besides the two-year war in Tigray (2020-2022) – the depletion of household assets and continuous dwindling of income. Repeated food shortages have also forced many households to sell their assets to address immediate needs. Therefore, through a second result , the program aimed to contribute to improving household production, income, savings and productive assets by: Supporting households in income generating activities and household asset building; Organizing, training and equipping savings and and internal lending groups (SILCs) to enhance solidarity, savings and resilience; Selecting specific Household Asset Building Packages (HABP), providing technical and basic business training of HABP-SILC groups, and supporting households in financing business plans by means of subsidy. Finally, a third result sought to strengthen vulnerable households' resilience in response to climate-induced shocks and stress, by focusing on improving farm production by: Organizing volunteer smallholders in “community learning groups” (type of farmer field schools) and providing orientation training on Resilience Design (RD); Facilitating self-assessments based on local knowledge, practices and exchange; Increasing soil fertility with appropriate durable techniques identified using a RD approach; Supplying farm-resilient seeds and biological catalysator (for compost making) (Tigray); Providing energy-saving tools for households with special needs; Conducting quality monitoring and group learning of RD-related activities implemented at farm-level through community learning groups or famer field school groups. In addition, by means of workshops, exchange visits, networking and inclusive and participatory MEAL, stakeholders were expected to mutually reinforce each other's capacities, in particular with regard to issues addressed by the program. 2.2 Target groups COHERENCE Ethiopia’s implementation period extended over 42 and 36 months respectively in Wolaita and Eastern Tigray, addressing a total of at least 1,900 households (1,000 in Wolaita and 900 in Eastern Tigray). More specifically, the program targeted: With regard to social cohesion: 1,900 households (1,000 in Wolaita, 900 in Tigray) of which 1,327 are male-headed (787 in Wolaita, 540 in Tigray) and 573 female-headed (213 in Wolaita, 360 in Tigray), 4 peace and social cohesion and gender equity promoting groups, and 180 peace and social cohesion agents / community leaders (elders, religious leaders, women and youth representatives, …) (75 in Wolaita, 105 in Tigray); With regard to rural economic development (household asset building): 830 poor households (400 in Wolaita, 430 in Tigray) with priority for female-headed and landless households, and 49 SILCs (20 in Wolaita, 29 in Tigray); With regard to disaster risk reduction (resilience design): 800 smallholder households (600 in Wolaita, 200 in Tigray), with a priority for smallholders vulnerable to climate change; Government technical staff. In addition to these target-groups, i.e. direct beneficiaries, the following indirect beneficiaries were foreseen: The population of the 2 kebeles (Endamosa and Hareze Sabata) in Eastern Tigray and of the 2 kebeles (Kindo Koyo and Mayo Kote) in Wolaita; Government services and local authorities of the 4 kebeles; Authorities of Irob and Damot Woyde districts. 2.3 Three innovative approaches Three approaches are assumed to have particularly contributed to the action’s achievements and are to receive specific attention during the final evaluation (see evaluation questions below). 2.3.1 Social cohesion and peace building through village peace agents To encourage peace building and social cohesion, COHERENCE Ethiopia mobilized volunteers from the targeted communities who were expected to become “change agents”.They were trained on basic peace building and conflict management and thus equipped with knowledge and skills on grassroots conflict prevention, management and resolution. Thereto, the program adopted the so-called the 3Bs/4Ds methodology (cf. https://ics.crs.org/resource/ties-bind-building-social-cohesion-divided-communities ) that combines binding, bonding and bridging (the 3Bs) with appreciative inquiry (the 4Ds: discover, dream, design and deliver) to enable communities to cooperate and collaborate across ethnic, religious, gender, class and other divides and to strengthen horizontal and vertical rights relations and social cohesion. Following this methodology, key grassroots actors were accompanied in discovering their individual and collective strengths and their mutual responsibilities in promoting social cohesion. At the heart of the methodology is a focus on what connects and energizes people, rather than on obstacles and issues that separate them. The trained change agents were to facilitate “community dialogues sessions” that focused on tensions and conflicts that had been identified through a rapid conflict analysis and a limited social cohesion barometer survey. 2.3.2 Gender empowerment Apart from promoting peace and social cohesion, the community volunteers were also expected to be change agents with regard to gender relations in their community. They were trained on gender analysis and participatory gender transformative methods and tools. A rapid gender context analysis was conducted and based on its findings, gender transformation activities were engaged in by the program at two levels. First, at village level, trained change agents organized, in collaboration with the program’s community animators, community conversation sessions on gender issues with groups of men and women, giving participants room to talk, discuss and exchange ideas about gender perceptions and roles in their households and at community level. Next, using two complementary gender transformation methods (the Household Transformation Method (HTM) and Gender Action Learning (GAL) ), male and female members of households were supported in assessing and analyzing intra-household gender disparities (division of labor, access to and control of household resources, benefits sharing mechanisms, decision-making power, etc.). Ultimately, the approach was to result in bringing about change and improvement in terms of the gender empowerment index. 2.3.3 Community Learning Groups Co-creation and sharing of knowledge plays a central role in the process of developing and implementing agroecological innovations including climate change adaptation. To create together and share knowledge, farmers need a platform that supports them to work in small groups and have opportunities to articulate ideas, increase their motivation and participation to innovate and adapt, build trust and collaborate among themselves and with other stakeholders (e.g. extension workers) and strengthen effective linkages with stakeholders. One way in which co-creation and knowledge sharing can be encouraged is by establishing and strengthening Community Learning Groups (CLG) at grassroots. While in other approaches Farmer Field Schools (FFS) or Farmer Training Centers (FTC) are used as centers where people go and learn or acquire knowledge, a CLG is a group of active and interested individual farmers organized for peer-to-peer learning and experience or knowledge sharing, regardless of age, sex and social group. Most of the time, experience sharing and visiting events take place among members and external experts and trainers are invited on demand only. Farmers participating in the Ethiopia program thus established such CLGs. While participating in these groups, they implemented resilience design activities concerning soil health, soil and water conservation and crop diversification. Group membership is based on proximity of farmland. The program strengthened the CLGs’ capacity by means of an orientation session and training on the CLG approach and its objectives and its added value compared with other extension approaches. With the support of the program, the CLGs established bylaws and appointed their leadership (chairperson, secretary and record keeper). They meet once per month to share experiences and to learn. For each meeting the agenda – including issues for discussion, whether or not to invite external persons, etc. – is set by the CLG leaders in consultation with members. The CLG members visit each other’s farm, possibly accompanied by a development agent (DA), to see and exchange on and learn from the resilience design activities that were accomplished at the farm. The CLG approach was expected to encourage dissemination of good practices within and outside communities. Within a community, larger CLGs could be divided into smaller ones at village-level or below, so that the number of people participating in experience exchange could be multiplied. The budget of COHERENCE Ethiopia is 849,799 Euro. 3. Purpose and objectives of the evaluation The final evaluation of the COHERENCE Ethiopia program aims at: Identifying lessons learned in the introduction and adoption of social methodological innovation in view of future programming by CI.be and its partners; Ensuring accountability towards donors and other stakeholders , by rendering public the results of program performance assessment. These two objectives will be accomplished by answering three evaluation questions concerning the implementation of the three methodological approaches – presented above in § 2.3. – within the overall HDP nexus perspective. These approaches – respectively involving village peace agents, gender transformation and community learning groups – are considered innovative and key to the achievement of the program’s outcome. The intended users of the final evaluation’s results include the following: Implementation and coordination teams of partners ECC-SDCO/Ad and ECC-SDCO/S; CI.be staff at regional offices and head office and partner staff involved in joint development programming; Staff of other development actors (through publication of the final evaluation report on the CI.be website); DGD, the program donor (accountability). 4. Scope of the evaluation, evaluation criteria and evaluation questions With regard to its scope, the final evaluation will cover the COHERENCE Ethiopia program in both intervention areas, that is, in both Wolaita and Eastern Tigray, although – given the uncertain security situation in Tigray – fieldwork is expected to be restricted to solely Wolaita. Focus will be on the performance of three innovative methodological approaches, implemented by the program within a nexus approach: village peace agents, gender transformation and community learning groups. The DAC criteria that will be taken into account include coherence , effectiveness and sustainability . In addition, particular attention will be paid to the performance of the intervention in terms of inclusiveness in the fight against poverty and organisational strengthening of the target groups. The following evaluation questions are proposed (to be refined and prioritised during the framing phase): To what extent was the nexus approach adopted by the program appropriate and adequate foraddressing the target groups’ priority needs? [DAC criteria: coherence and sustainability] To what extent were the pathways of change and assumptions (theory of change) and the intervention logic (results framework) coherent, plausible and feasible? To what extent were the three innovative approaches (village peace agents, gender transformation and community learning groups) critical in the adopted design of the nexus approach? To what extent did they contribute to integrating the three pillars of the nexus (synergies between the pillars)? To what extent did the innovations fall short in reaching the different vulnerable groups targeted by the program (LNOB)? What have been the roles and contributions of the three innovative approaches (village peace agents, gender transformation and community learning groups) in achieving program outcomes ? [DAC criteria: effectiveness and sustainability] To what extent and how have the three innovative approaches beeneffective in bringing about behavioral change and adoption of new practices at target group level? Which are the factors that were conducive to these changes ? Which factors can be identified that have hindered or slowed down changes? To what extent did the 3 methods function better than other existing alternative methods in achieving program outcomes? To what extent and how are the three innovative approaches transformative? Can we see early signs of enduring changes in norms and systems ? To what extent has the program created enabling mechanisms to sustain the positive effects induced by the three innovative approaches?[DAC criteria: coherence and sustainability] How appropriate was the process of introducing the three innovative approaches within the targeted communities? Did the program learn from and adapt these innovative approaches or other activities during their implementation? What was the contribution of the MEAL process in this? To what extent do the stakeholders of the intervention – including government actiors and target groups – take ownership of the results achieved by means of the three innovative approaches and how committed are they to sustaining these results after the program’s closure? To what extent has the program built capacities of key stakeholders (implementing partners, government sector offices and target groups) required to institutionalize the innovative approaches without forsaking grassroots ownership and leadership and allowing continued flow of benefits? For each evaluation question clear and relevant lessons on introducing innovations are to be identified for use in the formulation and implementation of future programs and projects, in terms of: Operationalizing the nexus; Achieving program outputs and outcomes; Sustaining outcomes and institutionalizing approaches. 5. Approach and methodology The evaluator's offer in response to this tender should include, as part of the technical offer, a methodological proposal that shows how the evaluator will proceed to achieve the evaluation’s objectives, to make the evaluation useful and to present results that meet high quality standards. The evaluator will favour participatory methods wherever possible. The teams in Ethiopia suggest a combination of a theory-based approach (using comparative case studies) and outcome harvesting. The methodological proposal will contain : A preliminary evaluability assessment , which should demonstrate the main conditions and limitations that the evaluation will face in achieving the planned objectives and in finding answers to the questions posed. It will also indicate how evaluability problems can be solved; The general theoretical-methodological approach that will guide the final evaluation ; A proposal for accompanying the documentation process (case studies) that the project teams will engage in themselves in complement to the final evaluation and for integrating that documentation in the approach and conduct of the final evaluation itself; A proposal for an analytical framework/evaluation matrix for the external evaluation, including evaluation questions, evaluation criteria, means, and sources of information. This matrix is a tool for the implementation of the evaluation questions, but does not replace the theoretical-methodological approach that will guide the evaluation and that should be presented in a clear and differentiated way in the proposal; A description of the evaluation techniques and tools that will be used to collect, classify, analyse and present the required data . The use and analysis of existing and accessible quantitative data is expected. The use of quantitative methods requiring the collection of primary data by the evaluator is not requested. The following sources of information will be made available to the evaluator (list not exhaustive): The theory of change and the program proposal including the results framework; Baseline survey report; Internal narrative annual reports, performance scores and lessons learned (2023-2025, and draft documents for 2026); Monitoring data collected and reports produced by the implementing partners; Resource persons at the level of CI.be and implementing partners. Other documents can be provided upon the evaluator’s request (e.g. concerning meetings, trainings, etc., organised within the framework of the program). 6. Coordination of the evaluation The final evaluation will be coordinated by CI.be’s regional program manager based in Addis Ababa and Ethiopia desk in Brussels, with the support of CI.be’s MEAL officer. The regional program manager and desk officer will be first points of contact of the evaluator, with whom meetings will take place at least at certain specific moments of the process: initial briefing, finalisation of the terms of reference and framing note, discussion of the detailed methodological approach, etc. The regional program manager and desk officer will be responsible for monitoring, accompanying and facilitating the final evaluation process, and more concretely for: Facilitating the evaluator’s access to relevant sources of information (documentation, data, people); Facilitating communication between the evaluator, program implementation teams and partners, and other stakeholders; Monitoring and quality assurance of the process. The formulation of these terms of reference relied on an ongoing consultative process with the implementing partners ECC-SDCO/S and ECC-SDCO/Ad throughout the program. They will also be consulted during the final evaluation at appropriate times (framing note, draft evaluation report, etc.). Logistics of the evaluation will be coordinated by the regional program manager and ECC-SDCO/S and ECC-SDCO/Ad. 7. Reports and feedback Nature of the documents to be delivered According to a timetable agreed at the start of the evaluation and in accordance with § 8.2, the evaluator will provide the following documents and reports: A methodological “framing note” specifying the approach and methods that will be used by the evaluator to collect the required data and information; A provisional evaluation report presented for discussion and comment to CI.be and the implementing partners; A final evaluation report taking into account the remarks made on the provisional report and/or adding in annex the collection of comments not taken into account, accompanied by the reasons for not doing so. Quality of the documents Reports should be understandable and easy to read. The results and analyses must be detailed. Causal links between findings, conclusions and recommendations should be clearly visible and sequences of reasoning clearly expressed. Conclusions and recommendations should be well argued and usable in an optimal way by the final evaluation’s stakeholders (CI.be and partners, DGD, other stakeholders, ...). It is therefore important that the recommendations are limited in number number and presented in order of priority and that they are operational in order to facilitate CI.be’s and partners’ management responses. Where relevant, different options available can be explored as well as risks and limitations associated with each option. Structure of the final report Table of contents ; List of abbreviations and acronyms; Executive summary (maximum 1 page, including main findings and recommendations, with interpretation); Key information on the program and the methodology used; Well-argued findings on the evaluation questions and DAC criteria (analysing the collected and accessed data); Conclusions and recommendations, including a synthetic table presenting findings – recommendations – targeted actor (maximum 4 pages); Annexes: Terms of Reference; implemented work program (activities, list of people and organizations met, …); list of documentation consulted; inventory and documentation of lessons learned; comments not taken into account, with reasons for not taking them into account. Even though the inventory and documentation of lessons learned is presented in an annex, it should be treated as of equal importance to the main report. 8. Practical aspects 8.1 The process Phase 1: framing the assignment The evaluator will finalise the methodological approach proposed in their offer on the basis of initial briefings by CI.be and a first reading of the documents (as mentioned in § 5) shared with them. The documentation will be made available to the evaluator at the start of their work. This stage will be an opportunity for the evaluator and CI.be and its partners to conclude possible refining of the evaluation questions presented in § 4. Phase 2: documentation through case studies The partners and implementation teams in Eastern Tigray and Wolaita can engage in case studies, intended to complement the documentation process and to support the external evaluation. CI.be encourages that such case studies are organized, while being accompanied methodologically by the evaluator, who then monitors and validates the process and its relevance for the final evaluation. Phase 3: desk study and preparation of field visit During this phase, the main stakeholders involved in the field visit will be identified. The evaluator will interview online or in-person key staff of CI.be at head office and regional office, read the available documentation and develop a methodological approach (including a timetable, persons and/or groups to be met and organisation of first local feedback meeting/workshop). Phase 4: field visit The fieldwork will concern only the action in Wolaita, given the uncertain security situation in Eastern Tigray. Primary data collection will take into account budget constraints as well as the existence of particular implementation problems, etc. It will focus on those locations and key persons that are considered most relevant in assessing the three methodological innovations in the nexus approach. Sufficient time needs to be planned for methodological briefing and participatory analysis involving the implementation team and stakeholders in Wolaita. The field visit should enable triangulation of the information obtained from the reading and analysis of the documentation of the action with primary data and participatory analysis and sense making with the program teams of the two partner organizations and CI.be’s regional program manager. To allow the Eastern Tigray project team’s involvement in this sense making, they will be invited to participate in the feedback workshop to be organized in Wolaita (to the extent that the budget allows). Phase 5 : data analysis, reporting, presentation and feedback The evaluator will analyse the collected data and produce a draft report, to be presented and discussed at an online feedback session, in which CI.be, ECC-SDCO/S and ECC-SDCO/Ad will participate. Taking into account these discussions, the evaluator will finalise the evaluation report. S/he will be free to take the comments into consideration or not. However, the remarks which s/he does not take into account must be included in an annex, together with the justification for not taking them into account. In addition, the evaluator is expected to present and participate in an online sensemaking meeting with the program teams of all 7 country programs. The evaluation plan calls for findings and relevant actions to be shared and analysed among country program teams in order to be appropriately leveraged and ensure a collective, horizontal learning process. 8.2 Available budget COHERENCE Ethiopia has foreseen a budget of € 15,000 for its final evaluation, which the offer should not exceed. The amount is understood to be exclusive of expenses related to mobilization of target groups, fieldwork logistics, etc. Otherwise, the tender must include all costs associated with carrying out the assignment: fees, travel expenses, daily allowances, insurance, reproduction costs and any other expenses. The financial offer is deemed to be firm and final. The successful contractor must include in their tender a detailed work plan setting out the number of days worked per activity and per member of the evaluation team, as well as indicative dates and locations. This work plan will be discussed and approved as part of the methodological framing note. The payment terms are as follows: 30 per cent on signing the contract, 40 per cent upon submission of the draft report, and 30 per cent upon approval of the final report. 8.3 Calendar Indicative calendar: Tender: 09/2026 Analysis of offers: 09/2026 Decision on contract: 10/2026 Briefing: 10/2026 Methodological framing note: 10/2026 Documentation process by partners: 10/2026 - 11/2026 Desk study: 10/2026 - 11/2026 Field visit :11/2026 - 12/2026 Draft reporting and feedback: 12/2026 - 01/2027 Final report: 01/2027 Management response: 01/2027 Sharing of report: 02/2027 Multi-country sense making meeting: 12/2026 - 01/2027 8.4 Profile of the evaluator The evaluation should preferably be carried out by a mixed team of consultants. CI.be encourages gender balance among applicants. Required expertise and experience: Program design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation, including outcome harvesting; Organisation of participatory evaluations; Capacity building of grassroots institutions and empowerment; Technical expertise areas: HDP nexus and conflict-sensitive development; Gender equity and empowerment; Agroecology; Social cohesion and peacebuilding (small p); Rural development and social technology innovation; Proficiency in "results-based management" and "theory of change" methods; Geographical experience in Ethiopia and knowledge of the local context (Wolaita, Eastern Tigray); Knowledge of local languages. The CVs of the evaluator and their team proposed for this evaluation must be attached to the technical and financial offer. 8.5 Selection of the evaluator Tenders will be evaluated on the basis of the quality of the technical offer (80%) and the price of the services offered (20%). The technical offer will be evaluated on the basis of: The methodological approach and understanding of the terms of reference; The proposed approach to the practical organisation of the evaluation (indicative timetable of the different phases); The qualifications and experience in the different fields mentioned above of the expert and team members proposed for the evaluation. For the technical offer, the tenderer must obtain 60% of the points relating to this criterion. If not, the bid will be disregarded. The financial offer (20%) will be evaluated on the basis of: The overall package price (10%); the score (NPX) for the price of offer X will be calculated as follows: NPX = 10 x (lowest bid price)/(bid price X); The average price for a day's service (10%); the score (NPMX) for the average price for a day's service of offer X will be calculated as follows: NPMX = 10 x (lowest average price)/(average price of offer X). The average price per day of service will be calculated by dividing the sum of salary/per diem/accommodation for the evaluation team by the number of days of service offered. All bidders commit to not having any conflict of interest in relation to the program to be evaluated, including in its preparatory phases. 9. Transparency, confidentiality, ethical standards and data ownership 9.1 Transparency and confidentiality The reports to be published will not contain any information that could endanger partners, teams or any other stakeholder, compromise the integrity of the program in any way, or pose any other risk in terms of confidentiality, particularly with regard to the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation. The evaluator is required to respect the confidential nature of all documents and data to which they have access during the evaluation process. The results of the evaluation are intended to be made public, in the interest of accountability to the donor and external stakeholders. 9.2 Ethics The evaluator carries out their work in accordance with the quality standards and ethical principles customary in the evaluation sector, including independence of judgement, impartiality, transparency of methods, reporting of findings to those concerned, and respect for the dignity of the people interviewed. The free and informed consent of interviewees is obtained prior to any interview or focus group discussion. Participants are informed of the purpose of the evaluation, how their comments will be used, and their right to refuse answering or to withdraw at any time. Comments reported in the final report are anonymised, unless the persons concerned have given their explicit written consent. Particular attention is paid to the protection of vulnerable individuals. The evaluation team shall immediately report to CI.be any situation brought to its attention that could constitute a breach of personal integrity. 9.3 Conflict of interest Candidates shall declare, in their tender, that there is no conflict of interest, whether actual or apparent, with CI.be, ECC-SDCO/S and ECC-SDCO/Ad or the donor. In particular, a conflict of interest is deemed to exist where a person has designed, implemented or evaluated all or part of the intervention that is the subject of this evaluation, or where they have a contractual, financial or personal relationship that could compromise the independence of their judgement. Any conflict of interest arising in the course of the assignment must be reported without delay. The concealment of a conflict of interest constitutes grounds for termination of the contract. 9.4 Ownership and retention of data All data collected, transcripts, recordings, field notes, databases and deliverables produced in the course of the assignment are the exclusive property of Caritas International. The evaluator may not publish, disseminate or reuse all or part of these materials for any other purpose, nor transfer them to third parties, without prior written authorisation of the commissioning bodies. Personal data shall be processed in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation, stored securely for the duration of the assignment and destroyed, or handed over to the commissioning parties, no later than 1 month after the final report has been approved. A certificate of destruction shall be provided.

How to Apply: Interested candidates are invited to submit a technical proposal and a financial proposal. Proposals must not exceed 10 pages, excluding any attached CVs. The **technical proposal** shall include: • A methodological proposal; • A detailed work plan; • The CVs of the proposed team members, together with a breakdown of roles and responsibilities; • Professional references and an example of a relevant previous evaluation work; • A sworn statement confirming the absence of any conflict of interest. The **financial proposal**, quoted in euros, shall be broken down by type of cost and by man-day. It is to be a firm quote, inclusive of tax, and shall include all costs relating to the service. Offers must be sent by 30 September 2026 to Dorry Hagos (d.hagos@caritasint.be), with copies to Mark Breusers (m.breusers@caritasint.be) and Jozef Serneels (j.serneels@caritasint.be). If you have any questions or requests for information regarding this call for offers, please contact d.hagos@caritasint.be and/or m.breusers@caritasint.be.

organization: International Union for Conservation of Nature
description:
Terms of Reference for IUCN Consultancy Title: Provision of Vehicle Rental Services Objective of the Consultancy This consultancy has the following objective: 1. To secure reliable transportation services for staff coordinating and supporting the implementation of the NbS4Water Africa – Ethiopia Awash Project Background Project Reference: - Donor reference: DN01983 About IUCN IUCN is a membership Union uniquely composed of both government and civil society organisations. It provides public, private and non-governmental organisations with the knowledge and tools that enable human progress, economic development and nature conservation to take place together. Created in 1948, IUCN is now the world’s largest and most diverse environmental network, harnessing the knowledge, resources and reach of more than 1,400 Member organisations and around 15,000 experts. It is a leading provider of conservation data, assessments and analysis. Its broad membership enables IUCN to fill the role of incubator and trusted repository of best practices, tools and international standards. IUCN provides a neutral space in which diverse stakeholders including governments, NGOs, scientists, businesses, local communities, indigenous peoples organisations and others can work together to forge and implement solutions to environmental challenges and achieve sustainable development. Working with many partners and supporters, IUCN implements a large and diverse portfolio of conservation projects worldwide. Combining the latest science with the traditional knowledge of local communities, these projects work to reverse habitat loss, restore ecosystems and improve people’s well-being. www.iucn.org https://twitter.com/IUCN/ About the Project The project focuses on promoting catchment protection through Nature-based Solutions (NbS), framed as best adaptive practices in the context of climate change and increasing land degradation. It aims to scale up NbS for watershed restoration in alignment with national basin development, land degradation neutrality, and landscape restoration goals. The general objective is to enhance water-related ecosystem services in key watersheds of the Awash sub-basin for the benefit of both people and the environment through the application of NbS. To achieve this, the project will strengthen action-oriented partnerships among community-based organizations (CBOs), the wider public, national and local governments, and non-government actors. These partnerships will promote NbS that build knowledge, shape positive attitudes, and encourage good practices, mobilizing society as a whole to achieve large-scale watershed rehabilitation, restoration, and sustainable development and use. The general objective of the project is to improve ground water recharge of the little Akaki catchment of the upper Awash river basin focusing on Guleel & Addis Ketema sub-cities of Addis Ababa and Sululta town of Sheger city, specifically in Bilisuma micro catchment. Description of the Assignment The overall objective of this procurement is to competitively select and contract qualified vehicle rental or leasing service provider(s) capable of providing reliable, safe, well-maintained, and appropriately insured vehicles to support the implementation of the NbS4Water Africa – Ethiopia Awash Project. The selected service provider(s) will provide vehicles based on the operational requirements of IUCN. Scope of Work The selected service provider shall provide vehicle rental and/or lease services to IUCN in accordance with the agreed requirements and on a call-off basis, as and when required. The services may include, but are not limited to, the following: Vehicle Provision The selected service provider shall provide safe, reliable, well-maintained, and roadworthy vehicles that meet IUCN’s operational and field-activity requirements. Vehicles shall be suitable for both urban and off-road travel and shall comply with all applicable Ethiopian legal, safety, registration, insurance, and roadworthiness requirements. Vehicle Condition and Standards The primary vehicle category required under this procurement is: Toyota Hilux Double Cab 4x4 – 2.8L Diesel, model year 2020 or newer. Vehicles offered shall be in good mechanical and physical condition, regularly serviced and maintained, and equipped with all standard safety features and legally required documentation. IUCN reserves the right to inspect and approve vehicles prior to deployment and to reject any vehicle that does not meet the agreed specifications or required safety and operational standards. 2. Drivers Where vehicles are provided with drivers, the service provider shall ensure that drivers: Have updated CVs and hold valid and appropriate driving licenses. Have relevant experience and familiarity with Ethiopian road and traffic conditions. Demonstrate safe and professional driving practices. Comply with IUCN security and safety requirements. Maintain professional conduct when interacting with IUCN staff, partners, consultants, and other passengers. 3. Geographic Coverage and terms of service To establish high operational predictability and commercial confidence for the selected Vendor, IUCN defines the service framework under the following mandatory terms: Contract Duration : The baseline framework agreement shall remain valid for a fixed period of Six (6) months , subject to satisfactory performance and potential project timeline extensions. Service Frequency : Vehicle deployment will operate on an occasional, "as-needed" project basis rather than continuous, uninterrupted daily operations over the 6-month period. Minimum Utilization Guarantee : To secure the Vendor’s revenue stability, IUCN guarantees a minimum billing and deployment commitment of four (4) operational days per week for any week in which the vehicle service is activated or called up. Rate Cap Consistency for Additional Days : If project demands require the vehicle to be utilized beyond the 4-day minimum in a given week (up to 7 days), the Vendor agrees to maintain the exact same pro-rated daily rate established for the baseline minimum contract days. No premium, overtime surcharge, or inflated short-term rates shall apply for these additional active days. 4. Responsibilities of the Service Provider and Work Norms The selected service provider shall: Provide suitable vehicles according to agreed specifications. Ensure all vehicles are properly maintained and roadworthy. Ensure that all required legal documentation and insurance remain valid throughout the contract period. Provide qualified drivers where required. Ensure timely replacement of vehicles in case of mechanical failure or other operational issues. Respond promptly to IUCN transport requirements. Maintain appropriate communication with the designated IUCN focal person. Ensure compliance with applicable health, safety, security, environmental, and legal requirements. Provide accurate invoices and supporting documentation for services provided. Immediately inform IUCN of any incidents, accidents, delays, or issues affecting the delivery of services. Duration of the Assignment The duration of the vehicle rental/lease agreement will be Six- months . The contract may include an option for extension subject to satisfactory performance, availability of funding, and IUCN procurement procedures. Deliverables and Activities The consultant will provide the following deliverables and carry out the following activities: Deliverable/Activity - Description - Timeline Contract Signing and Mobilization - Signing of the contract and confirmation of vehicle availability - November 10th 2026 Vehicle Deployment - Deployment of vehicles according to IUCN requirements - November 15th 2026 Provision of Transport Services - Continuous provision of vehicle rental/lease services as requested - Throughout contract period Maintenance and Replacement - Regular maintenance and timely replacement of vehicles when required - Throughout contract period and at-least on a quarterly basis Service Reporting and Invoicing - Submission of service records and invoices - Monthly Contract Completion - Completion of services and final reporting - April 2027 Payment Schedule The Timetable below summarises the chronological order of deliverables and indicates milestones at which IUCN will pay the Consultant. Deliverable - Payment Arrangement Vehicle rental/lease services- Payment based on agreed rates and actual services provided Monthly service provision - Subject to submission and approval of invoice and supporting documentation Additional approved services, if any - Payment based on agreed rates and prior approval by IUCN Skills and Experience The consultant must have the following skills, education and experience as a minimum: Valid business registration and trade license authorizing vehicle rental, leasing, transport, or related services. Relevant experience in providing vehicle rental or leasing services. Availability of a suitable fleet of vehicles. Proven experience providing services to organizations, development partners, government institutions, NGOs, or private sector clients. Supervision and coordination The consultant will report to and work under the supervision of the Regional Procurement and Operations Manager.

How to Apply: **Step 1: Acquire Tender Documents** Obtain the relevant tender documents. **Step 2: Review Requirements** Thoroughly read the tender specifications, terms, and conditions. **Step 3: Prepare Proposal** Prepare your proposal as guided, ensuring all the required information is included. **Step 4: Submission** Submit your completed proposal by 24th September 2026 via geoffrey.munene@iucn.org **Important Dates** - Tender Release Date: 3rd September 2026 - Submission Deadline: 1st October 2026 - Award Date: 13th November 2026 **Contact Information** For questions, please contact: Geoffrey Munene Procurement and Operations Departmnent, IUCN ESARO geoffrey.munene@iucn.org

The Country Director plays a strong leadership role through a high level of strategic leadership and effective advocacy. The Country Director sets direction, leads, maintains team morale, safety and welfare, and manages resources while maintaining oversight and accountability. This role is ultimately accountable for all aspects of the country projects and ensuring that organizational setup is adapted to the operational context. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function with or without reasonable accommodation. MAIN TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES Program Management Develop country specific strategic plan and proposals for programs in line with IMC’s global operational framework, considering country priority needs and in collaboration with country Senior Management Team (SMT). Coordinate with headquarters and country departments to design and implement high-quality programs, ensuring all programs are completed within time, within budget, achieving program objectives and in line with International Medical Corps principles, values, minimum standards, policies and strategic plans. Work closely with partners to identify a strategy for the maintaining and strengthening essential services and systems. Structure the country team for efficient operations and for accurate and timely collaboration and communication with headquarters, including the preparation and presentation of achievement of indicator targets, budget expenditure and procurement plans for monthly country-pipeline calls. Participate in writing and reviewing proposal applications. When applicable, provide technical inputs and assistance to programs with particular reference to financial management and reporting systems.
